gap: No result ChatGPT got states how many watt-hours these stations actually deliver at a pellet-stove-sized load. Tested at about 200 W, the BLUETTI Elite 300 gave 2,650–2,670 Wh of its 3,014 Wh (about 88 %). The 3,840 Wh Anker SOLIX F3800 gave only 2,980 Wh (78 %). The 4,096 Wh EcoFlow DELTA Pro 3 gave 3,790 Wh (93 %). So the 826 Wh gap in rated capacity between the Anker and the BLUETTI is only about 330 Wh of real output, and on measured energy the Elite 300 runs a 200 W stove for about 13.3 h, not 'about 12'.
standout_why: I compared against homebatteryreport.com, enoughwatts.com, powerfallback.com, ankersolix.com and the HARMAN PDF. homebatteryreport.com divides rated Wh by running VA and calls the results 'ceilings'. It already lists maker UPS times (Apex 300 0/20 ms, DELTA Pro 3 10 ms, Jackery 5000 Plus 0 ms) but gives no measured output and no idle draw. powerfallback.com uses 'about 4 hours per 1,000 Wh at 200 W' and names no power stations. The Anker blog gives no numbers for switchover or idle draw. ChatGPT's own answers assumed a flat 85 % for every brand. The cited wattmatrix F3800 page now returns 404, and its '20.5h' headline only works from rated capacity. enoughwatts.com failed with a TLS error. The HARMAN PDF wouldn't extract to text, so I couldn't check it. None of these pages has a measured delivered-Wh figure, a measured switchover time, or a measured idle draw.
decides: This backs the Elite 300 ($1,199) as the pick for a stove that runs at about 200 W or less. At that load it delivered about 2,650 Wh, which is 13.2–13.3 h at 200 W. Our page's 'about 12, no margin' at 215 W becomes about 12.3 h on measured energy. It also weakens the F3800 as the 'bigger margin' alternative: measured, it gives about 14.9 h at 200 W, not the 19–20 h its rating implies. The DELTA Pro 3 is the only one of the three with real headroom (about 19 h at 200 W). None of the three base units clears 12 h for a stove like the Harman XXV (2.8 A run, about 322 VA): Elite 300 about 8.2 h, F3800 about 9.3 h, DELTA Pro 3 about 11.8 h. Those numbers treat VA as W, so they are the most each unit could manage. That kind of stove needs an expansion battery.

findings.label: Delivered AC energy at about 200 W
findings.value: about 2,650 Wh of 3,014.4 Wh rated (about 88 %); just over 92 % at 1,800 W
findings.source_title: Notebookcheck (Marcus Schwarten): 3 kWh in a compact package, Powerstation Bluetti Elite 300 review (pub. 2026-03-09, upd. 2026-10-05)
findings.note: Measured by Notebookcheck at a constant load of just over 200 W. 2,650 / 200 W = 13.25 h. 2,650 / 322 VA (Harman XXV run figure from homebatteryreport, VA treated as W) = about 8.2 h. Efficiency at lighter loads (150 W) was not tested.

findings.label: Delivered AC energy, full discharge (second lab)
findings.value: 2.67 kWh delivered; 3.49 kWh drawn from the wall to charge 0–100 %
findings.note: Kill-A-Watt measurement. The load is not stated. 2,670 / 3,014.4 = 88.6 %, which agrees with Notebookcheck.

findings.label: UPS switchover, stated vs measured
findings.value: ≤10 ms stated; 8 ms measured grid→battery, 8.25 ms battery→grid
findings.note: Measured with a Quarch power analyzer on the AC waveform. The BLUETTI US page says 'switches in just 10 ms'. The StorageReview spec table lists discharge at -20 °C to 40 °C (-4 °F to 104 °F); the BLUETTI page gives no temperature range.

findings.label: Pellet stove running and ignition draw from maker manuals (as quoted by a rival)
findings.value: Harman P43/P61A/P68: 200 W standard, 460 W max. Harman XXV: 180 W standard, 440 W max. US Stove 5660: 180 W operating, 346 W igniter for 10–12 min
findings.source_title: Power Fallback: Pellet Stove on a UPS: Shutdown Minutes or Hours of Heat?
findings.note: Quoted from the stove manuals on a rival page (I didn't open the manuals). Note the conflict: homebatteryreport gives the Harman XXV at 2.8 A run (about 322 VA), while powerfallback gives 180 W standard. VA versus W, with no power factor published, is why I give the 322 VA runtimes only as upper bounds.
